title: Sperm Whale: The Loudest Animal on Earth
description: The sperm whale produces the loudest clicks on Earth at 236 decibels and has the largest brain of any known animal. Its single S-shaped blowhole sits asymmetrically on the left side of its head.

beats.text: The sperm whale's head is filled with wax.
beats.visual: Sperm whale surfacing in open ocean, large head prominent above water

beats.text: That waxy substance is called spermaceti, and by reflecting sound, it helps the sperm whale become the loudest animal on Earth.
beats.visual: Sperm whale skull showing spermaceti organ, museum specimen display

beats.text: Its clicks reach 236 decibels underwater. No other animal on the planet comes anywhere close to producing that sound.
beats.visual: Hydrophone array deployed from research vessel measuring underwater sound

beats.text: The whale fires those clicks while diving to 7,380 feet in the deep open ocean.
beats.visual: Sperm whale diving steeply underwater, body angled downward into darkness

beats.text: It also has the largest brain of any known animal, whether modern or extinct.
beats.visual: Sperm whale brain specimen displayed next to human brain for scale

beats.text: But to surface for air, it has a unique S-shaped blowhole on the left side of its head.
beats.visual: Sperm whale skull showing S-shaped blowhole on left side, museum specimen

beats.text: That's why the loudest animal on Earth fills its head with wax.
beats.visual: Sperm whale surfacing, blowing water from left-side blowhole into sky
queries: sperm whale surfacing left side blowhole
